mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the federal funds rate above 4% over the prior month reduces the discount rate applied to future corporate cash flows, lowering the present value of expected earnings and thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns in the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by 0.5 percentage points over the past month
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during a similar rate-unchanged month (p > 0.05 in t-test).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) coinciding with a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which raises consumer confidence and equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 4% while PAYEMS increases by 10,000 or more in a month
failure_condition: 20-day test of positive return significance fails (p > 0.05) or employment growth decelerates while unemployment rises in the subsequent month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in personal consumption expenditures (CPIAUCSL) above 0.2% inflation-adjusted growth for three consecutive months indicates accelerating demand, which anticipates higher corporate profits and supports S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day rolling mean of 20-day forward returns remains below the 1-year average (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) and a sharp drop in the ratio of orders to shipments (not directly observable here, but proxy via supply chain stress indicators) suggests weakening manufacturing capacity, which depresses equity valuations and predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by 2% in a month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS exceeds 5%, the expected discount rate for equities rises, reducing the present value of future earnings and driving negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days in a tightening cycle.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive and statistically significant (p < 0.05) during the tightening period.

mechanism_narrative: A regime shift to a labor market tightness environment where monthly job openings (not directly observable but proxy via employment growth and unemployment rate dynamics) outpace job separations predicts sustained wage growth and corporate hiring, which supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE remains below 4% while PAYEMS growth exceeds 5% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns show no outperformance versus a baseline of stable labor conditions (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 3% for three months suggests the Federal Reserve may maintain current policy, reducing policy uncertainty and allowing equity valuation to stabilize and produce positive 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative and statistically significant (p < 0.05) during the low-inflation period.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls for three consecutive months while the ratio of new orders to capacity utilization (not directly observable but inferred from supply chain stress) deepens, it indicates an emerging supply shock that depresses corporate earnings expectations and yields negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases in three consecutive months
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) or INDPRO recovers in the following month.
